text: A subgraph pattern that recurs in a network far more often than expected in randomized networks of the same degree sequence (assessed via a z-score) is called a network ___.
explanation: Such statistically overrepresented subgraph patterns are called network motifs; examples in E. coli's regulatory network include the feedforward loop and bi-fan. The z-score compares the real count of a subgraph to its average count in an ensemble of randomized networks that preserve the degree sequence (the configuration model), with a z-score above about 2 used as the threshold for overrepresentation.
